about: Thresholds for the search versus category comparison. scripts/category_match.py reads this file, so change a rule here and nowhere else. Each key is explained under notes.

notes.top_queries: How many of the busiest search queries (by browse sessions) are checked for a matching category.
notes.min_sessions: Queries with fewer browse sessions than this are skipped: too little traffic to judge.
notes.page_size: How many products count as page one when comparing the search and category grids.
notes.overlap_aligned: If at least this share of the category's page one also appears on the search page one, search and category are aligned: no action.
notes.overlap_low: If less than this share of the category's page one appears on the search page one, the pages are mismatched.
notes.broader_ratio: Search counts as broader than the category when it finds at least this many times as many products (numFound).
notes.perf_gap: The category beats the search (or the other way round) when its conversion rate is better by at least this share, e.g. 0.15 = 15% better. Revenue per visit is used when conversion is missing.
notes.brand_shift: A brand mix difference (total variation distance, 0 to 1) at or above this is flagged.
notes.price_ratio: A median page-one price on one page at least this many times the other's is flagged.
notes.stock_gap: An in-stock share on the search page lower than the category's by at least this much (0 to 1) is flagged.
notes.stock_fields: Product fields read as stock (true/false, 'in stock'/'out of stock', or a number above 0). Ask for one of them in the grid fl. If none is returned, the stock check is reported as not checked.
notes.department_words: Words in a query that name a top-level department, keyed by the department's name in the category path. 'mens pants' matches /men/pants, not /women/pants.
